mechanisms.name: append-only-jsonl-event-log
mechanisms.what: Session holds an in-memory append-only `SessionEvent[]` written only by `Session.append` (packages/core/session/src/index.ts:703-754): each call snapshots `data` as lossless JSON, validates the event payload and surface metadata, freezes the envelope, and pushes it, so the event's `seq` is exactly the pre-push log length. The JSONL backend serializes those events one JSON object per line after a `type:'session'` header record (`eventLines`/`eventLine`, session-persistence-jsonl/src/format.ts:312-323) into an immutable generation file `session.v<N>.jsonl` (optionally checksummed Zstandard frames), extending it with `persistBatch` (index.ts:807-821) or materializing a fresh generation. Cold reads decode the artifact through a bounded parsed-log handoff memo (`COLD_LOG_MEMO_MAX_ENTRIES = 2`) and one fail-closed validation pass (`decodeStoredLog`, index.ts:711-768).
invariants: Committed events are never rewritten and seq is contiguous from 0, equal to the log length (the `seq = log.length` contract)
Every event's `data` must be losslessly JSON-serializable; violations throw at the append site rather than at flush time
One JSON object per event row, with the header as exactly one JSONL line, so a physical tail is truncatable at a record boundary
mechanisms.failurePolicy: fail-closed — non-JSON payloads, invalid surface metadata, and reentrant appends throw before the log mutates (index.ts:713-735); unreadable artifact bytes become SessionPersistenceCorruptionError (index.ts:751)
constants: SESSION_FORMAT_VERSION = 3 stamped into every header line (packages/core/session/src/types.ts:88)

mechanisms.name: seq-contiguity-and-branded-sequence-types
mechanisms.what: Sequence positions are nominal types rather than bare numbers: `SessionSeq` admits only non-negative safe integers that are existing event positions and `SessionLogOffset` admits the same for gaps/prefix lengths/cursors, both rejecting `-0` (packages/core/session/src/types.ts:30-58). Contiguity is enforced at three boundaries with the same rule: the Session constructor refuses a seed whose `seq` differs from its index (index.ts:570-572), every append derives `seq` from the log length, and the persistence seam re-checks batches with `assertContiguous(id, events, cursor)` before writing (session-persistence/src/storage-contract.ts:145-151).
invariants: Stored and live logs are dense from seq 0; a gap is never representable except through the explicit `SessionLogOffset` gap/prefix type
A seed, fork prefix, or append batch must continue the stored next-seq exactly
`-0` is not a valid sequence value anywhere (JSON-unstable negative zero)
mechanisms.failurePolicy: fail-closed — TypeError from the brand constructors, `seed event at index N has seq M (expected N)` from the constructor, and `append seq mismatch` from assertContiguous

mechanisms.name: surface-projection-and-derived-history-cache
mechanisms.what: The model-visible conversation is a projection over the event log rather than a stored field: message-producing events carry a `surfaceOp` (`'append'` or `{op:'replace',startSeq,endSeq}`) and `sourceEventSeqs` (packages/core/session/src/types.ts:434-450), and `SurfaceManager.validateNext` accepts each candidate before it enters the log. `Session.deriveMessages()` walks the ordered surface nodes and folds the pure per-node rule `deriveEventMessage` (surface.ts:92-126), caching each node's projection exactly once and rebuilding only when the surface's `replaceGeneration` changes (index.ts:825-846). The same exported fold is reused by external reconstructors so a rebuilt transcript equals what the request was built from.
invariants: Derived history comes only from surface nodes; a raw event without a marker never enters the transcript
A replacement node must cite every shadowed surface node and must cover their ranges completely
The derived cache is invalidated by surface rewrite, and returned arrays are fresh snapshots while their Message objects stay shared and deep-frozen
mechanisms.failurePolicy: fail-closed — surface metadata and request-header/tool-error consistency are validated in `validateSessionEventData` and `validateNext` during append, so a bad event never enters the log

mechanisms.name: session-fork-inherited-prefix
mechanisms.what: `SessionStore.fork(source, boundary, childSessionId)` creates a live child from a stable prefix of a live source: the boundary must be an existing inclusive seq and must not end inside an open turn, otherwise typed `SessionForkError` codes are raised (index.ts:1196-1254, codes at 870-875). The child records `inheritedEventCount` = the copied prefix length and an `isSeeded` header, and the constructor appends a tagged `session/end-seed` marker at the inherited cut (index.ts:606-610) so a later reader can tell inherited history from live work; `ownEvents()`/`isOwnSeq()` expose the cut (index.ts:648-659).
invariants: The fork boundary is an inclusive, existing, contiguous seq and never lands inside an open turn
A seeded session's constructor seed length must equal its declared inherited prefix length, and an unseeded session's inherited count must be 0
The inherited cut is durable in the log (last tagged `session/end-seed`), not only in memory
mechanisms.failurePolicy: fail-closed — SessionForkError with codes SESSION_NOT_FOUND, SESSION_NOT_LIVE, SESSION_ALREADY_EXISTS, INVALID_BOUNDARY, OPEN_TURN
constants: Fork error codes: SESSION_NOT_FOUND, SESSION_NOT_LIVE, SESSION_ALREADY_EXISTS, INVALID_BOUNDARY, OPEN_TURN (packages/core/session/src/index.ts:870-875)

mechanisms.name: crash-repair-torn-tail-and-interrupted-turn-closers
mechanisms.what: Crash recovery has a physical half and a semantic half. Physically, the JSONL reader never returns a torn tail: it records `tornTruncateTo` (and, for Zstandard, the complete records recovered from a torn final frame as `recoveredTail`), and the write path truncates the torn bytes with fsync and durably rewrites recovered events before the handle's first new append (index.ts:736-739, 840-844, 1287-1296; storage.ts:328-337). Semantically, `interruptedTurnClosers(events)` synthesizes deterministic closers — error `tool/result` events for unmatched calls (codes TOOL_NOT_STARTED / TOOL_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN), then any open `step/end`, then `turn/end {reason:{kind:'interrupted'}}` — reusing the last event's timestamp; resume appends them through the write handle as an ordinary batch, and read-only observers balance a cold log in memory only.
invariants: A torn physical tail is discarded and fsynced before any new append, so duplicate seq numbers can never be written
Synthetic closers are the only crash story: an interrupted turn is closed, never resumed in place
Closer synthesis is deterministic (reuses the last event's time) and only runs for a log whose tail turn is open
mechanisms.failurePolicy: mixed — a torn-tail repair that fails rejects the append (fail-closed), while a balanced/empty log yields no closers and unmatched-call repair degrades into explicit error results the model can read

mechanisms.name: write-lease-and-lazy-materialization
mechanisms.what: A created session is visible to this process immediately but has no filesystem footprint: `create` registers a pending entry and returns a handle with `materialized:false`, and the session materializes on its first append or on an explicit flush (index.ts:308-327; storage.ts:203-212). Write ownership is claimed in two stages — an in-process claim at write-open (`tracker.claimWrite(id)` / `pendingOf`, index.ts:340-366) and a cross-process kernel lock acquired lazily right before the first materializing write (`ensureLease`, storage.ts:345-354). The lock is a non-blocking `flock(2)` on `session.lock` inside the session directory, or a Windows named kernel semaphore derived from that path, so a crashed holder never blocks a successor and no expiry can expropriate a live writer.
invariants: At most one active writer per session id — in-process claim plus kernel lock; readers never touch the lock
An unmaterialized session has no durable artifact, so a crash before first materialization means the session never existed
A POSIX lock names an inode, so after locking the holder must verify the locked inode is still the file at the lock path
mechanisms.failurePolicy: fail-closed — SessionAlreadyOwnedError on contention (EBUSY on Windows, EAGAIN/EWOULDBLOCK on POSIX); a failed write-open releases both the kernel lock and the in-process claim before rethrowing

mechanisms.name: write-behind-batching-and-flush-barrier
mechanisms.what: Persistence is split into a best-effort append feed and an explicit durability barrier. Published events are routed by session id into a per-handle buffer that drains through the handle's mutation chain after a bounded batching window (`LIVE_WRITE_BATCH_MAX_DELAY_MS = 200`, storage.ts:36, 274-316); a drain failure retains the batch in order and pauses the timer so a later flush can retry loudly. The barrier is `session/flush`: the backend handles it by draining the routed buffer then flushing the handle (storage.ts:534-547), `SessionStore.flush(session)` awaits every listener in parallel and rethrows the first rejection (core/session/src/index.ts:1137-1154), and the service-wide `flushAll` aggregates per-session failures into an AggregateError (storage.ts:508-523).
invariants: Only a resolved flush promises durability; a resolved append is merely accepted, ordered, and visible to later reads on the same backend instance
A failed drain must retain the buffered events in order rather than dropping or reordering them
An empty created session becomes durably listable only through flush (handle.flush materializes a header-only artifact)
mechanisms.failurePolicy: mixed — append is best-effort and background drain failures are logged with the buffer retained; the flush barrier is fail-closed (first listener rejection is rethrown; service-wide flush raises AggregateError)

mechanisms.name: semantic-checkpoint-policy
mechanisms.what: `session-checkpoint-policy` converts the raw flush barrier into semantic durability checkpoints by wrapping three boundaries: `llm/stream` defers adapter dispatch until `ctx.sessions.flush(session)` resolves for the complete logged request prefix (index.ts:29-38, 64-68), `tools/execute` flushes the recorded call before a top-level tool body runs (index.ts:70-75), and `agent/pre-step` flushes everything the preceding step committed (index.ts:79-82). Nested tool dispatches deliberately reuse the durable outer call.
invariants: A checkpoint rejection must prevent the downstream adapter or tool body from running
Only top-level tool dispatches checkpoint (exec.parent must be undefined)
Checkpoints happen before side effects, not after, so a crash cannot leave an unlogged side effect
mechanisms.failurePolicy: fail-closed at both side-effect boundaries — a rejected flush means the model call or tool body is never invoked; a tool call cancelled after the checkpoint is answered with a canonical aborted result

mechanisms.name: session-format-adjacent-migration-chain
mechanisms.what: A session log declares one monotonic logical format version (`SESSION_FORMAT_VERSION = 3`) that is bumped only for structural changes; every historical generation keeps its own physical codec and one adjacent migration edge (v0->v1, v1->v2, v2->v3). `defineSessionFormatMigration` rejects a non-adjacent edge and `CompiledSessionFormatChain` compiles the complete inventory at construction time, failing if any `vN->vN+1` step for `0..currentVersion-1` is missing, duplicated, or leads past the current version (chain.ts:24-34, 50-87); a stored version selects a precompiled contiguous slice and an unsupported/newer version produces a status or typed refusal rather than a partial read. The shipped instance is generated build-static in `session-format-catalog` with all four codecs and all three edges wired directly, so historical readability does not depend on mounted plugins.
invariants: Migration edges are adjacent, uniquely named, and complete from v0 to the build's current version — no gaps, no dynamic lookup
Both sides of every edge must agree: the chain is only valid when an older writer's codec and the edge chain are compiled together
Filenames encode the generation: version 0 is `session.jsonl`, later generations are `session.v<N>.jsonl`
mechanisms.failurePolicy: mixed — header classification is fail-soft (returns a `current | migration-required | unsupported | malformed` status object), while restore, encode, and every migration step are fail-closed with SessionFormatError / SessionFormatUnsupportedMigrationError
constants: catalog currentVersion = 3, codecs v0/v1/v2/v3, migrations v0->v1, v1->v2, v2->v3 (packages/session/session-format-catalog/src/generated.ts:14-18)

mechanisms.name: generation-migration-publication
mechanisms.what: A historical generation is never rewritten: migration streams the source through the adjacent chain into a staged temp file, verifies the staged file's bytes and sha256 digest in an isolated Worker Thread against the expected id and event count, re-checks the source's physical identity (`dev:ino:size:mtime:ctime`) to detect a concurrent writer, and only then publishes the new current generation with `link()` (deliberately not `rename()`, so two processes cannot clobber each other) followed by a directory fsync (generation.ts:879-938, 812-838). If the link reports EEXIST, the competing current file is validated instead — it must match the staged bytes/digest — so concurrent migrations converge on one winner. Without a current generation, a legacy `session.jsonl` is migrated and adopted rather than rewritten.
invariants: Immutable generations: migration writes a new file and never mutates the historical source
Publication is exclusive and no-clobber (link fails with EEXIST); a lost race is resolved by validating the winner, not by overwriting
Staged bytes/digest must equal the verified bytes/digest before publication and the source identity must be unchanged after verification
mechanisms.failurePolicy: fail-closed — digest/identity mismatch, worker failure, or a non-collision filesystem error rejects and removes the staged temp; a cleanup failure joins the primary failure in an AggregateError

mechanisms.name: unknown-event-vocabulary-refusal
mechanisms.what: The append-only log is merge-extensible, so a reader that meets an event type it does not know must refuse rather than silently skip it unless the writer marked the event `ignorable: true` (packages/core/session/src/types.ts:473-483). The build publishes its vocabulary as a generated 56-entry set `KNOWN_SESSION_EVENT_TYPES`, and `validateStoredEvents` refuses any stored event outside that set that lacks the marker, plus the one retired shape hiding under a known type (`request/header` with reason `"fallback"`), before adopting and freezing the events (session-persistence/src/storage-contract.ts:69-104). Writes are also constrained at append time by `assertSessionEventEnvelope`, which admits only the seven envelope keys.
invariants: Absent `ignorable` means required: an unknown required event must refuse the whole read, never be dropped
Vocabulary growth for purely informational records is expressed by the persisted `ignorable` marker, not by runtime event-name registration
Retired pre-release shapes under a still-known event type are refused explicitly
mechanisms.failurePolicy: fail-closed — SessionFormatUnsupportedError for unknown/retired vocabulary, SessionPersistenceCorruptionError for records that fail validation
constants: Envelope keys accepted by a write: type, seq, time, data, surfaceOp, sourceEventSeqs, ignorable (packages/core/session/src/index.ts:204-217)

mechanisms.name: projection-registry-checkpoint-restore
mechanisms.what: `ctx.sessionProjections` drives per-session derived state: a domain registers a unit (key, zod state schema, pure `init`/`apply`, optional wire view, `stateVersion`) and the registry folds every committed `session/event` into every registered unit, notifying the change feed only when a unit's raw view changes by `Object.is` (session-projection/src/index.ts:199-223, 233-293). The same service is the read side of the persisted cache: `checkpoint()` emits detached `(ver, seq, val)` rows, `restoreFloor()` anchors a tail read one event below the lowest usable watermark so a shrunken log is detected, and `restore()`/`viewCheckpoint()` re-seed from version-matching rows and refold the tail (index.ts:396-435, 448-509). Consumers such as `sessionStats` and `turnOutline` supply only the pure fold and register it as an effect on their own fiber.
invariants: Unit functions must be synchronous and their state must be plain JSON — the persisted-cache precondition
A row is a fold shortcut, never authority: a `ver` mismatch, a malformed value, or a watermark past the stored log end discards it and refolds
Registration is fiber-owned: unloading a domain removes its key from snapshots, and a key shared by N registrants survives until the last one unloads
mechanisms.failurePolicy: mixed — registration conflicts and a discarded row with `baseSeq > 0` throw (fail-closed), while malformed or mismatched rows are skipped so a cold consumer sees the key as not-yet-available (fail-soft)
constants: Each unit declares a non-negative integer `stateVersion`; a mismatched or absent row pulls the restore floor to 0 (packages/session/session-projection/src/index.ts:270-272, 425-435)

mechanisms.name: projection-cache-write-behind
mechanisms.what: `SessionProjectionCache` persists the projection registry's checkpoints into the `session_projcache` storage domain on a throttled write-behind: a dirty counter plus a timer, plus three mandatory write points — session creation, every `turn/end`, and disposal (the live-to-cold moment) (session-projection-cache/src/index.ts:301-352). Each session document binds the checkpoint rows to a log identity (format version, createdAt, cwd, isSeeded, inherited cut) so a recreated id or a swapped persistence root cannot seed state folded from an unrelated log, and the domain is declared `layout: 'per-record'` so a bad document is discarded per session rather than bricking the medium.
invariants: The cached record is derived data only: a stale or unreadable record costs a longer tail replay, never a wrong value
Every write binds the rows to the session's log identity; identity mismatch means the record reads as absent
The write path flushes the log before persisting a checkpoint, so a cache record can lag the log but never lead it
mechanisms.failurePolicy: fail-soft — every durable write goes through `flushSoft`, which logs a warning and leaves the cache stale, self-healing on the next write; a cold-read write-back is fire-and-forget with a logged warning
constants: domain spec: name 'session_projcache', version 7, compatibleVersions [3,4,5,6], invalidRecords 'backup-and-skip', layout 'per-record' (packages/session/session-projection-cache/src/spec.ts:98-105)
writeEveryEvents = 200 and writeIntervalMs = 5000 are required deployment config (packages/bundle/base/cordis.patch.yml:162-166)

mechanisms.name: session-lifecycle-ownership
mechanisms.what: `SessionStore` separates construction, entry, and announcement so publication is transactional: `prepare` builds a detached session (validating id, cwd, seed continuity and header fields), `enter` installs the module-private append/publication hooks and returns a detach disposer, and `announce` emits `session/created` exactly once (core/session/src/index.ts:962-1004, 1028-1062, 1083-1111). `create` folds the three into one generator effect owned by the calling fiber, so a synchronous throwing creation listener rolls the attach back with a paired `session/disposed`; a session published outside that lifecycle persists nothing. Append/announce reentrancy is refused, and detach requested during dispatch is deferred until the dispatch unwinds.
invariants: One store entry per session id: enter re-checks for a duplicate so a stale prepared session can never displace a live one
A synchronous `session/created` throw vetoes and rolls back with a paired disposal; an async rejection only logs
Detach during an in-flight announce/append is deferred, never executed mid-dispatch
mechanisms.failurePolicy: fail-closed — duplicate id, already-attached, double-announce, reentrant append, and operations on a non-live session all throw; observer failures are contained per listener and logged

mechanisms.name: versioned-kv-storage-domain
mechanisms.what: Session durability sits on a two-layer storage stack: a `storage` hub with a registry of named backends (json, sqlite) and a `storage-domain` facility that opens schema-validated, change-emitting KV domains with a per-domain declaration (`name`, `version`, `compatibleVersions`, `layout`, `invalidRecords`). The JSON backend publishes whole documents atomically — same-directory temp opened `wx` at 0o600, fsync of the file, `rename()` over the target, fsync of the parent directory on POSIX — and its per-record layout treats a malformed or version-unaccepted document as foreign (reads as absent) so one bad record cannot brick a unit. The SQLite backend stamps `PRAGMA user_version` last and rejects any non-current stamped layout, and all domain writes are ordered durability -> memory -> `domain/changed` emission on a single per-domain chain.
invariants: A domain's declaration is the single source of its identity, version, layout, and record schema; validation happens at module load
Per-record reads accept only the current version plus declared compatibleVersions; any other stamp is discarded, never migrated in place
A delivered write is atomic on the medium and durable once resolved; the unit does not serialize concurrent writers — ordering is the caller's chain
mechanisms.failurePolicy: mixed — fail-closed for open/config/version-mismatch and whole-unit layouts; fail-soft for per-record JSON (foreign/stale/unreadable documents read as absent) and for `invalidRecords: 'backup-and-skip'` (record moved aside as `<key>.json.bak.<stamp>`, error logged, domain opens without it)
constants: JSON atomic publish: temp `.<uuid>.tmp`, open 'wx' mode 0o600, file fsync, rename, POSIX directory fsync (packages/storage/storage-json/src/atomic.ts:24-40)
per-record document shape `{version, record}` serialized with 2-space indent + trailing newline (packages/storage/storage-json/src/format.ts:97-99)

mechanisms.name: session-telemetry-record-capture
mechanisms.what: `ctx.sessionTelemetry` is a backend-agnostic record seam over the canonical log: a coordinator mirrors each committed event as one ledger record (deep copy of `data`, a redaction waterfall `session-telemetry/record`, then a non-blocking `emit`) and adds ops records for `agent-error` and shutdown, with a module-scope `handoffCursor` WeakMap advanced only when a record is handed over (session-telemetry/src/coordinator.ts:92-124, 151-162). Live capture is the default and installs listeners on session creation, disposal, event, flush and agent error; the shipped OTel backend instead uses `{capture:'on-demand', includeHistory:true}` and releases a prefix only when explicit feedback authorizes it, exporting OTel log records (not spans, not metrics) through a `LoggerProvider` + `BatchLogRecordProcessor` + OTLP/HTTP exporter with a backend-owned shutdown deadline.
invariants: Capture must never alter or rewrite the canonical session log; redaction applies to the exported copy only
A capture failure withholds exactly one record and never reaches the agent loop (per-record containment)
Only feedback authored by this session (seq >= inheritedEventCount) authorizes an OTel upload; fork-inherited feedback does not
mechanisms.failurePolicy: mixed — each record is contained fail-closed (a throwing listener or backend error logs and skips that record); backend shutdown rejection is caught and logged; the OTel plugin fails closed at load on invalid exporter/processor config
constants: deployment: exporter.timeoutMillis 1000, processor scheduledDelayMillis 10000, maxQueueSize 2048, maxExportBatchSize 2048, exportTimeoutMillis 1500 (packages/bundle/base/cordis.patch.yml:188-197)

mechanisms.name: llm-backed-session-title
mechanisms.what: `ctx.sessionTitle` folds the last `session/title` event into a client-visible `title` projection (stateVersion 1) plus a host-only `titleInput` unit, and exposes a single-slot provider registry; a provider receives the eligible human messages and returns a title plus the cited `messageSeqs` (session-title/src/index.ts:263-292, 295-311). Cadence is data-driven, not timer-driven: an eligible `user/message` records a pending revision and the model call starts only once the exact request route is logged, with a revision counter plus AbortController superseding stale work. Two model providers ship: `session-title-first-prompt-llm` (registered as the base-bundle row id `session-title-llm`, automatic = first-prompt) and the opt-in `session-title-all-prompts-llm`; the shared policy package appends a log-only `session/title-llm-request` event before dispatch.
invariants: A title is durable state in the log, not mutable metadata: readers fold the latest `session/title` event
Only one provider may be registered per service; a second registration is refused
A stale revision's result must never commit — supersession is checked before the append
mechanisms.failurePolicy: mixed — explicit callers (`rename`, `refresh`) get fail-closed SessionTitleInvalidError and service-disposed errors, while the automatic path contains provider failures, logs a warning, and keeps the deterministic fallback title
constants: title-LLM policy (no library defaults): targetWords 5, targetCjkCharacters 10, maxInputBytes 4096, maxOutputTokens 64, timeoutMs 60000 (packages/bundle/base/cordis.patch.yml:57-62)

mechanisms.name: session-controller-remote-facade
mechanisms.what: `SessionController` owns the generated `ctx.remote.session` namespace and is the host-side read/dispatch facade over the session domain: list, search, create, selectModel, modelCatalog, openWorkspacePath, rename, fork, prompt, attachment, updateQueue, cancel, page, follow (stream) and control (stream), plus sibling `skills` and `fileReferences` namespaces (api/session-controller/src/index.ts:121, 222-225). It never writes the log itself — reads go through `ctx.sessionQuery` (`observeSession`, `listSessions`, `traceSession`) or `ctx.sessions.get()` + `snapshotEvents()`, and history paging is message-aligned with a backward cursor (`page`, history.ts:77-111). Background activation is the promote step: after a cold snapshot is delivered, an observation is handed to the agent controller in a tracked promise whose failure is logged rather than surfaced.
invariants: No controller operation writes the session log or dispatches `session/flush`; durability stays with the agent loop and persistence backend
Every request is validated (address, page range, through-cursor) before any storage read
Cold reads must not activate an agent; activation is a separate, tracked promotion step
mechanisms.failurePolicy: mixed — request/address/state failures throw typed RemoteError codes (session/not-found, session/conflict, session/agent-busy, gateway/bad-request, subagent/unauthorized, ...), while background promotion failure and projection-lookup failure are logged and degrade

mechanisms.name: cross-session-reference-snapshot
mechanisms.what: `sessionReferenceResolver` injects another session's projected conversation into the live one as untrusted, read-only context: an `agent/pre-step` prepend hook parses `@[label](dsh-session:...)` mentions out of direct user messages and places each prepared snapshot immediately after the message that cited it (context/session-reference/src/index.ts:127-142, 298-355). The snapshot is read from persistence via `ctx.sessionQuery.readSurface(sessionId)` — never from a live Session object — and is budgeted: a per-source UTF-8 limit derived from the model context window (4 bytes/token heuristic) with a 64 KiB floor, oldest-first whole-message dropping, then head/tail truncation of the longest message; a truncated preview carries omission facts plus a spilled full-transcript locator when spill storage is composed.
invariants: The referenced content is untrusted and read-only: it never becomes durable history of the source session and never mutates persistence
A reference to the receiving session itself is refused, and at most MAX_REFERENCES sources are accepted per message
A preview that omits text must advertise the omission (bytes, whole messages) and locate the full transcript or state that it is unavailable
mechanisms.failurePolicy: fail-closed via SessionReferenceError codes (INVALID_CONFIG, INVALID_REFERENCE, SELF_REFERENCE, TOO_MANY, READ_FAILED, BUDGET_EXCEEDED, CANCELLED), with fail-soft degradation for optional spill storage (unavailable notice) and for a missing model context capacity (falls back to the default byte budget)
constants: spilled transcript fragments text at 64 Unicode code points per line (packages/context/session-reference/src/spill.ts:77)

mechanisms.name: deepseek-session-log-contribution
mechanisms.what: `session-log-deepseek` ships the canonical log suffix to the official DeepSeek API as a request field: it registers a `dsh_session_log` contribution whose value carries `version: 1`, the session format version, wire header, `afterSeq`/`throughSeq` and the events after the last accepted watermark, and its `accept` callback appends a `session-log-deepseek/delivery-accepted` event back into the canonical log (src/index.ts:157-191). The watermark is folded incrementally from those acceptance events with a WeakMap cache (`acceptedThrough`, index.ts:117-150), so restart recovery can conservatively resend an uncertain tail without a second store. The plugin is registered in production compositions but `enabled` defaults to false, and no shipped bundle row sets it, so the contribution is inert there.
invariants: The acceptance watermark lives in the canonical log; no separate delivery store exists
A delivery-accepted event must name this session, reference an earlier seq, and carry a well-formed format version — otherwise it is a malformed log
Unaccepted suffixes are resent; accepted prefixes are never re-sent
mechanisms.failurePolicy: fail-closed on read (throws on a missing event below the captured length, a malformed acceptance format version, or a malformed watermark), with degrade-to-undefined when the request has no session id or the session is not live

moduleCoverage.util/atomic-write: Contributes none to the session domain: the session log backend implements its own temp+fsync+link()+dir-fsync publish in session-persistence-jsonl and does not import @deepseek-ai/dsh-atomic-write; this package's writeFileAtomic/withFileLock consumers are settings-file, credentials-local, agent-presets, profile boot and llm-deepseek upload-index, and it explicitly declares crash durability (fsync) out of scope (packages/util/atomic-write/src/index.ts:73).
moduleCoverage.util/crypto: Contributes none to the session domain: randomUUID/bytesToBase64 serve gateway/client/inspector/llm message-id minting; the session packages use node:crypto directly (session-persistence-jsonl hashing/temp names) or brand their own ids. It is stateless utility code with no session-log, locking, or durability role.
moduleCoverage.test-support/session-snapshot: Contributes none to a production session mechanism: it is a test-tier subprocess snapshot harness (harvests persisted session JSONL, normalizes, diffs with toEqual/toMatchFileSnapshot) and is explicitly declared to mount nothing into a product composition; its session-format filename helpers are test-side readers of the same generation naming convention.

notes: Scope: session domain of dsh v0.1.5-rc.2, read-only audit; no file in the source tree was modified. All evidence lines were opened with the read tool in this session (verified:true everywhere); a few structural statements come from parallel read-only reconnaissance and are attributed to the same packages.
